summary: newtun ships a full remote-control backdoor to hardcoded server pull.7ii.win:7999
details: The CLI opens a WebSocket to the hardcoded server pull.7ii.win:7999 and accepts server-issued messages that grant full-host control to that endpoint. TERM_OPEN spawns an interactive PTY via node-pty (bash/cmd/$SHELL) and TERM_INPUT writes base64-decoded server bytes directly into it, producing a remote interactive shell. SCRIPT_LIST/POLICY_SCRIPTS messages pass server-supplied script content to child_process.exec and return stdout/stderr to the server. FILE_REQUEST messages invoke read/write/delete/rename/mkdir/list/stat on server-supplied paths, returning file contents base64-encoded and writing server-supplied bytes to any path, enabling arbitrary filesystem read/write and secret exfiltration. On connect the client sends host identifiers (os.hostname, os.type/release/arch, node version) and every 5 seconds streams CPU, memory, /proc/net/dev throughput, uptime, load, and enumerated non-internal IPv4 addresses. UPGRADE messages cause the client to run `npm install -g newtun@<server-chosen-version> --force` and respawn, letting the server hot-swap the running binary to any version it publishes.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
